beats.head: Blackmoor Inches Higher as Ridge-Till Attachment Lifts Holloway Range
beats.body: Blackmoor reported revenue of $196M, up 4%, with the new ridge-till attachment lifting attach rates on the Holloway seed-drill range past 40%. CEO Soren Dray, in his characteristically unhurried tone, emphasized multi-season durability data over near-term volume. The company reaffirmed its slow-build outlook into next planting cycle.

beats.head: Caldercraft Holdings Edges Ahead as Weatherproof Range Fills Out
beats.body: Caldercraft posted a modest beat with revenue of $288M, up 6%, as the completed weatherproof line — racks, cabinets and reinforced fittings — lifted average order size across hardware channels. CEO Vale Fenn described demand as 'steady and unremarkable, in the best sense,' pointing to consistent reorder patterns from regional distributors.

beats.head: Carrowcyon & Sons Tops Estimates as Third Smart-Dimming Line Comes Online
beats.body: The 130-year-old house reported quarterly revenue of $412M, up 19% year over year, as its newly commissioned third production line began clearing a backlog of national retail orders. CEO Cole Brandt credited disciplined ramp-up, noting attach rates on companion lighting fixtures rose to 34%. Margins widened 210 basis points as scale absorbed the earlier capacity crunch.

beats.head: Carrowforge Returns to Profit as Renn's Post-Split Machines Unit Steadies
beats.body: Carrowforge swung back to a $31M quarterly profit from a prior loss, as newly appointed Machines Chief Tobias Kade trimmed overlapping product lines and cut lead times by 18%. CEO Dahlia Renn called the quarter 'proof the split was worth the pain,' though she cautioned that legacy Roe-era divestitures remain incomplete. Order intake for industrial presses rose 12% sequentially.

beats.head: Cranecraft Runs Streak to Thirteen as Planting-Season Orders Peak
beats.body: Cranecraft extended its consecutive-beat streak to thirteen quarters, with revenue of $344M as farm-equipment orders crested with the planting season and textile pricing held firm. CEO Mira Garr noted the streak now spans more than three years, crediting balanced exposure across farm and raw-textile lines. Backlog stood at a record $210M.

beats.head: Gromford Works' Reinforced Emblem Collection Takes Guild Design Honor
beats.body: The relaunched Emblem Collection won the Continental Craft Guild's annual accessories citation, a reputational lift for CEO Halvard Pryce after the earlier clasp recall. Judges praised the reinforced clasp mechanism and enamel detailing. Pryce said the award 'closes the book' on a bruising launch cycle and vowed a broader Emblem expansion by year-end.

beats.head: Halhold Works Ships Aveline Successor to First Markets as Rocha's Reset Advances
beats.body: Halhold began commercial shipments of its redesigned device, the successor to the troubled Aveline line, into three initial markets under CEO Anselm Rocha's turnaround plan. Early orders totaled $85M, with Rocha touting a rebuilt medical-equipment interface and stricter component sourcing to distance the product from prior recalls. Rocha called the launch 'the first real test of whether the cleanup took hold.'

beats.head: Ornewright Goods Beats as Multi-Region Jansan Contract Begins Shipping
beats.body: Ornewright posted revenue of $267M, up 9%, as its recently won multi-region cleaning and janitorial supply contract began contributing shipments. CEO Petra Veldt said the deal added roughly $40M in annualized run-rate while farm-inputs demand stayed 'reliably flat.' Management guided for a fuller contract ramp over the next two quarters.

beats.head: Aperture Compute Faces Regulatory Probe Over Emberline Fabrication Site Conditions
beats.body: Regulators opened a formal inquiry into safety and environmental practices at Aperture Compute's Emberline fabrication sites following reports of ventilation and chemical-handling failures at the second facility now under construction. Marisol Venn said the company was cooperating fully and had paused some site work, but the probe casts a shadow over the $2.6 billion supply pact signed only weeks earlier. Shares tumbled on the news.

beats.head: Bruncraft Misses as Coachline Ramp Costs Outrun Vane's Guidance
beats.body: Bruncraft posted quarterly profit of $310 million, well short of the $420 million analysts expected, as tooling and labor costs tied to the Coachline flagship launch ran higher than forecast. Marcus Vane conceded that consolidating the Vanguard unit had absorbed more capital than planned but insisted the flagship's order book remained intact. Shares of the automaker have been volatile since the $1.8 billion buyout closed.

beats.head: Bruncrest Works Signs $3.4B Aria Ultra Framework, Its Largest Order on Record
beats.body: Ines Marlow announced a $3.4 billion multi-year framework agreement anchoring output from the new compute line, roughly tripling the size of the earlier landmark Aria Ultra order. The pact locks in dedicated capacity through the decade and validates Marlow's contested throughput bet. Deliveries are slated to begin once the newly broken-ground line reaches qualification.

beats.head: Dunmorewright Beats as Waterworks Billings Ramp Ahead of Schedule
beats.body: Dunmorewright reported revenue of $1.9 billion, topping estimates, as early billings on the $780 million inland waterworks contract flowed faster than projected. Emil Skarn credited the recently expanded foundry capacity for pulling delivery milestones forward by nearly a quarter. Management reaffirmed full-year guidance.

beats.head: Maison & Vale Unveils $4.2B Merger with Household-Goods Giant Larenthal in Kessler's Boldest Move
beats.body: Rhys Kessler capped an aggressive acquisition streak with a $4.2 billion agreement to absorb Larenthal Group, more than doubling the size of the company's Household Goods division. Executives said the combined operation would rank among the largest hospitality-supply houses by revenue, though integration costs are expected to weigh on margins for at least three quarters. The deal follows the Corriveau and Vestrand bolt-ons that steadied recent earnings.

beats.head: Varnvale & Sons Integrates Corvane, Doubles Complication Output at Reopened Movement House
beats.body: Bram Wold said the newly acquired Corvane Movement House has been fully brought in-house, doubling annual grand-complication capacity and easing the supply bottleneck behind the award-winning line. The company added forty master watchmakers and reopened a shuttered atelier wing to support the ramp. Wold hinted further movement-house talks remain on the table.

beats.head: Brunstone & Sons Lands $900M Fleet Supply Pact for Vault II Cells
beats.body: Brunstone secured a five-year, $900M agreement to supply Vault II cells to a national commercial-vehicle fleet operator, its largest single order since the recall crisis. Frost called the deal 'proof the comeback is real,' noting it effectively resolves the demand questions that lingered even after the class action; the pact commits Brunstone to a third assembly shift by next spring.

beats.head: Castlestone Misses Badly as Grid-Core Delays Bleed Into Guidance Cut
beats.body: Castlestone posted revenue of $2.1B against $2.7B expected, with the relaunched Grid-Core campus still running at 60% of rated capacity months after Karsh 'drew a line.' The house slashed full-year guidance by nearly a fifth and disclosed that two anchor Compute clients had deferred contracts, sending Karsh into a combative call where he vowed the setback was 'the last one.'

beats.head: Boreas Power Strikes $3.2B Deal to Build Compute-Paired Power Campuses Nationwide
beats.body: Mira Thorne announced a $3.2B agreement with infrastructure partner Delmar Holdings to co-develop six power-and-compute campuses over four years, pairing Boreas storage with Halvane-built modules at each site. The deal, the largest in company history, locks in long-term offtake commitments Thorne valued at more than $9B across the contract life. 'This is the model we bought Halvane to build,' Thorne said, calling it the culmination of her acquisition strategy.

beats.head: Greywater Grid Faces Regulatory Probe Over Closed-Loop Reservoir Discharge Claims
beats.body: Regulators opened a formal inquiry into Greywater Grid's closed-loop water figures after inspectors flagged discrepancies between reported and measured discharge at two reservoir sites. The probe casts a shadow over the $2.4B compute pact anchored to those facilities, portions of which include performance clauses tied to water recovery. Sable Renwick said the company 'stands fully behind its data' and is cooperating, but acknowledged the review could delay site certifications.

beats.head: Marlgear Supply Documents Show Executives Ordered Kessel Fault Records Destroyed
beats.body: Internal memos surfaced in the widening probe showing senior Marlgear leaders directed staff to purge Kessel fault logs weeks before regulators arrived, according to filings reviewed at a public hearing. Dane Kessler denied personal knowledge but placed two divisional heads on leave as the board opened an independent review. Shares of confidence cratered as the class action added the document allegations to its complaint.

beats.head: Vossenspire Supply Strikes $2.1B Deal to Acquire Rival House Corriveaux
beats.body: Quinn Marrow unveiled the largest acquisition in Vossenspire's century-long history, absorbing storied timepiece and coachbuilding house Corriveaux for $2.1 billion. The deal combines Vossenspire's Thelvane case works with Corriveaux's renowned movement ateliers, creating a top-tier luxury conglomerate. Marrow said the integration would 'complete the vertical chain from raw brass to boutique.'

beats.head: Castlehold Lands Landmark $2B Grid-Storage Framework, Its Largest Ever
beats.body: Halden Voss secured a multi-year framework worth up to $2B to supply high-capacity modular storage to a consortium of regional utilities, more than doubling the firm's existing backlog to over $3B. Deliveries begin next quarter and will require Castlehold to accelerate a planned third plant. The deal cements Voss's aggressive first-year expansion, though it also raises execution risk given how fast the order book has swelled.

beats.head: Halhold Systems Ousts Petra Vandel as Reliability Settlement Forces Board's Hand
beats.body: The board removed CEO Petra Vandel after regulators finalized a $650M settlement over concealed reliability failures, the largest penalty in the firm's history. Directors named restructuring veteran Marcus Thorne as chief executive with a mandate to rebuild oversight and stabilize a shaken customer base. The exit closes a scandal that spread from shareholders to regulators over three brutal quarters.

beats.head: Blackhold Ordered to Idle Second Storage Campus as Probe Widens to Design Flaws
beats.body: Regulators expanded their inquiry into the overheating incident, ordering Blackhold to fully suspend operations at the second storage campus while investigators examine a suspected thermal-management defect across multiple units. The shutdown jeopardizes roughly $1.2B in grid-mandate obligations, and CEO Halden Dabney faces mounting pressure after acknowledging the campus was brought online ahead of schedule. Officials said the campus will remain dark until independent certification, with no firm restart date.

beats.head: Calderforge Cuts Guidance as Fourth Stormwell Hall Delays Compound and Yields Falter
beats.body: Calderforge missed a second straight quarter and slashed full-year guidance as the fourth Stormwell hall ramp fell further behind and next-gen tier yields came in below plan. Nadia Throne conceded the house over-committed on capacity ahead of demand, and disclosed a charge tied to idled equipment. The turbulent update marks Calderforge's sharpest setback in years, with Throne pledging a cost review across the Stormwell footprint.

beats.head: Drayton Freight Wins Continent-Spanning Warehouse Automation Contract Worth $900M
beats.body: Drayton Freight landed its largest-ever award, a $900M multi-year deal to outfit a national warehouse operator with pallet-lift handlers and material-handling systems. CEO Emil Holt, in a rare bold stroke, said the contract secures both assembly plants at full capacity through 2029. Management expects it to lift Material Handling revenue by a quarter next year.

beats.head: Vossenspire Holdings Ousts Halden Roe as Storage-Bank Probe Turns Damning
beats.body: Vossenspire's board removed CEO Halden Roe after investigators found commissioning protocols on the failed grid-scale storage bank had been rushed against internal warnings. Director Mara Venn will serve as interim chair while the search proceeds, and the house suspended two further storage projects pending review. Shares have shed nearly half their value since the outage.
